data.name: Abraha
data.gender_notes: Abraha is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Abraha was the king of Yemen who led an army against the Kaaba in Mecca. This name signifies the bravery and determination of a father protecting his people and beliefs. The name Abraha carries the meaning “Father of Ishmael” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Abraha usually hope their child will grow to embody father of ishmael and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Abraha is a name that represents the strength and wisdom of a wise and just ruler. It is a name that carries the weight of history and tradition, and those who bear it are believed to have the courage and determination to overcome even the greatest challenges.
data.etymology: Abraha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Father of Ishmael.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abraha total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: أبرهة
in_arabic.long_meaning: أبرهة هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، ويعني القائد العسكري الإثيوبي الذي حكم مكة في فترة ما قبل الإسلام، وقد ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سورة الفيل، حيث كان أبرهة قد بنى كنيسة في اليمن ووجهها نحو مكة، فدعا الله أن يهديه إلى الطريق المستقيم، ولكن الله أرسل الطيور الأبابيل على أبرهة وجيشه فأهلكتهم

in_english.name: Abraha
in_english.meaning: Ethiopian military leader, ruler of Mecca
in_english.long_meaning: Abraha is a masculine given name of Arabic origin. It refers to an Ethiopian military leader who ruled Mecca. He is mentioned in the Quran, Surah 105 (Al-Fil), where Abraha built a church in Yemen and oriented it towards Mecca. As a result, God sent flocks of birds to destroy him and his army. The name Abraha symbolizes a historical figure known for his ambitious and sacrilegious act against the Kaaba.

data.cultural_impact: Abraha is remembered as the historical adversary of Prophet Muhammad's ancestor, Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). His attempt to destroy the Kaaba caused a significant event in Islamic history, leading to a deeper awareness and commitment to preserve the scared Islamic sites.

historical_references.reference: Abraha, the king of Aksum (Ethiopia), led an army to Mecca in 538 AD to destroy the Kaaba and spread Christianity. He was repelled by the combined forces of Mecca and Medina, led by Abul-Aas ibn Rabia and Muhammad bin Maslama al-Ansari.
historical_references.context: An attempt to destroy the Kaaba and spread Christianity

historical_references.reference: Abraha was a vassal king of Himyar in southern Arabia, and his Yemenite kingdom was a major power in the region during the 5th and 6th centuries. He was a Christian convert and sent an army to Mecca in 570 AD to suppress the Islamic faith and restore paganism. This event, known as the Battle of Mu'tah, was a turning point in the early Islamic history as it led to the first major military campaign of the Muslim community under Muhammad's leadership.
historical_references.context: An attempt to suppress the Islamic faith and restore paganism
